Notice of Privacy Practices acknowledgme.title: Notice of Privacy Practices — HIPAA and applicable substance-use privacy protections
Notice of Privacy Practices acknowledgme.summary: Effective November 2, 2026. Indian Creek Psychological Services, Inc., 15022 W. 128th St., Olathe, KS 66062. Privacy contact: Privacy Officer, 913-353-6116. You may request a paper copy and ask questions before acknowledging receipt.

parts.heading: Your health information; our duties
paragraphs: This notice explains how the practice may use or disclose protected health information (PHI) and how you can exercise your privacy rights. We are required to protect the privacy and security of your PHI, follow the notice currently in effect, provide you a copy, and notify you when a breach of unsecured PHI requires notice under applicable law.

Our records may include contact information, clinical evaluations, diagnoses, treatment plans, progress, medications, insurance claims, billing information and electronic communications. Special rules can apply to psychotherapy notes and certain substance-use disorder records.

parts.heading: Uses and disclosures usually permitted without a separate HIPAA authorization
paragraphs: Treatment: We may use and share appropriate information with health professionals involved in your care, subject to stricter laws when they apply. Payment: We may use information to verify benefits, submit claims, receive payment or resolve billing matters. Health care operations: We may use information for quality review, compliance, practice administration and authorized professional consultation.

The law may permit or require disclosure for public health and safety, reporting suspected abuse or neglect, serious threats to health or safety, health oversight, certain law-enforcement purposes, workers’ compensation, legal proceedings under valid authority, coroners and medical examiners, and other specifically authorized circumstances. We evaluate applicable legal requirements before disclosing.

Other uses may require your written authorization. We do not treat a privacy-notice acknowledgment or a general treatment consent as an authorization for unrelated disclosures. We will obtain separate authorization when required for marketing, sale of PHI or most uses or disclosures of separately maintained psychotherapy notes.

parts.heading: Your individual privacy rights
paragraphs: You may ask to inspect or obtain copies of records in the designated record set, including eligible electronic copies; request corrections to records; request confidential communications by alternative means or at alternative locations; request restrictions on certain uses or disclosures; request an accounting of certain disclosures; obtain a paper copy of this notice; and designate a legally authorized personal representative.

We generally may decline a requested restriction unless law requires us to honor it. For example, where HIPAA conditions are met, we must honor your request not to disclose information to a health plan for payment or health care operations when you have paid in full out of pocket for the relevant service. We will explain any lawful denial of a record-access or amendment request and available review rights.

You may raise questions or file a privacy complaint without retaliation. Contact the Privacy Officer at Indian Creek Psychological Services, Inc., 15022 W. 128th St., Olathe, KS 66062, telephone 913-353-6116; or complain to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights at hhs.gov/hipaa/filing-a-complaint or 1-877-696-6775.

parts.heading: Sensitive mental-health information, psychotherapy notes and Kansas confidentiality
paragraphs: We apply HIPAA and applicable Kansas confidentiality and privilege laws to mental-health records. Some disclosures permitted by HIPAA may be restricted by more protective state law. We assess subpoenas, court orders, mandatory reporting, personal-representative authority and other exceptions case by case rather than assuming every legal request permits immediate disclosure.

Psychotherapy notes are a narrow category of notes kept separately by the clinician to document or analyze counseling-session conversations. They generally require a separate authorization for use or disclosure, subject to limited legal exceptions. The separate psychotherapy-notes form in this packet is voluntary.

parts.heading: Additional safeguards when 42 CFR Part 2 applies
paragraphs: Indian Creek reports that it does not operate a Part 2 program. Some records received from outside substance-use programs can nevertheless remain subject to 42 CFR Part 2. When those rules apply, the practice will assess the source, scope and lawful basis before using or disclosing them. A routine intake signature does not itself supply a separate consent that law requires.

Part 2 records generally cannot be used or disclosed to investigate or prosecute a patient in civil, criminal, administrative or legislative proceedings without a qualifying patient consent or a court order that satisfies Part 2 and an appropriate subpoena or similar legal mandate. Recipients and redisclosures remain subject to the applicable limitations. Ask the Privacy Officer whether particular records are covered by Part 2 and for a Part 2-specific consent when needed.

Additional Part 2 rights, such as certain recipient lists and accounting rules, apply as provided in current regulations and their implementation schedules. Where HIPAA and Part 2 overlap, applicable protections govern rather than a blanket waiver in this notice.

parts.heading: Choices, changes and the notice itself
paragraphs: Where the law gives you a choice, you can object to certain family/friend disclosures or give or withdraw authorization as permitted. We ordinarily honor a valid written revocation prospectively; prior actions lawfully taken in reliance on an authorization cannot always be undone. A recipient who is not governed by HIPAA may be able to redisclose information, subject to other applicable laws.

We may change this notice and apply a revised notice to records we maintain to the extent permitted by law. Updated notices will be available at our office and website. This notice is available in paper or electronic form and is not a consent to treatment or an authorization to release records.

parts.heading: Requests, timing and acknowledgment
paragraphs: Ask the Privacy Officer how to submit an access, correction, confidential-contact, restriction or accounting request. HIPAA generally calls for action on an access request within 30 days, with a permitted extension explained in writing when applicable; amendment requests generally have a 60-day response period with permitted extensions. Applicable exceptions and more protective laws are assessed for the particular request. An accounting generally covers eligible disclosures during the preceding six years, with the first requested accounting in a 12-month period provided without a charge.

If fundraising communications are used, you may choose not to receive them. Where Part 2 information is involved, any required advance notice and choice must be provided. Nothing in this notice authorizes use of Part 2 records in proceedings against you without the consent or legal process that law requires.

The office requests a written acknowledgment that this notice was received or made available. You may decline that acknowledgment. Refusal to sign does not itself prevent treatment; the office must document its good-faith effort and why an acknowledgment was not obtained. A receipt acknowledgment is not a release of records or agreement to waive privacy rights.

Consent to Counseling and Informed Treat.title: Informed Consent for Counseling, Psychological and Substance-Use Services
Consent to Counseling and Informed Treat.summary: Please review the nature of services, limitations and alternatives with your clinician before deciding whether to consent.

parts.heading: Services and clinician qualifications
paragraphs: Services may include intake assessment, diagnostic interviewing, counseling, psychotherapy, treatment planning, psychoeducation, family or relationship work, substance-use assessment and relapse prevention, and referrals when appropriate. The services and frequency of sessions are determined collaboratively based on clinical assessment and available care.

Before treatment, the practice will identify the clinician providing services, relevant professional credentials, any supervision arrangement, proposed services and significant limitations. Counseling and addiction-treatment services do not by themselves authorize medical practice or medication prescribing. Medical or medication concerns may require referral to a qualified medical professional.

parts.heading: Benefits, limitations, risks and alternatives
paragraphs: Potential benefits include improved understanding, coping, relationships and functioning. Treatment can also involve uncomfortable emotions, reflection on distressing experiences, changing important relationships, or temporary worsening of symptoms. Specific outcomes cannot be guaranteed.

Alternatives may include choosing another clinician or treatment method, group or community services, medication evaluation by a qualified prescriber, higher levels of care or choosing not to participate. You can ask questions, participate in treatment planning, refuse a particular intervention or discontinue outpatient treatment subject to applicable legal and safety obligations.

parts.heading: Confidentiality and its limits
paragraphs: Treatment information is kept confidential as required by law. Limits can include suspected abuse or neglect reporting, appropriate response to threats of serious harm, medical emergencies, authorized health oversight, some valid legal process and other disclosures required or permitted by law. Couples, family and group services carry additional confidentiality considerations: other participants are not bound by the practice’s HIPAA duties, and joint-record or information-sharing arrangements should be discussed before treatment.

For minors or legally represented patients, we review the legal decision-maker’s authority, applicable minor-consent rules, records access and any limits on disclosure. A parent or partner does not automatically control every confidential detail. Coordination with other professionals is limited to what law permits or what you specifically authorize.

parts.heading: Appointments, crises and professional boundaries
paragraphs: This practice is an outpatient service and the website, portal, voicemail and email are not continuously monitored emergency channels. In an immediate emergency, call 911 or go to an emergency department; use your local crisis-response services when appropriate. Clinician availability, between-session contact and referral arrangements should be discussed directly.

Treatment sessions are professional clinical services. Contact outside visits, gifts, social media interactions, requests for written opinions, disability letters, court reports or testimony, and transfers of care must be discussed in advance; none is promised solely by signing this intake.

parts.heading: Separate choices and your decision
paragraphs: My choice below applies to the proposed outpatient services discussed with the clinician. It does not authorize recording, research, publicity, sale of information, disclosure of specially protected notes or any procedure requiring separate consent. I may ask for clarification or decline a proposed service. If I request discussion rather than consent, the practice must resolve the treatment decision before providing the relevant nonemergency service.

If I consent, I intend my dated electronic signature on this form to record that decision. Consent is an ongoing discussion; I may raise questions or withdraw from prospective voluntary treatment, subject to applicable safety and continuity obligations. A signature on another page is not substituted for this form.

Financial Agreement and Good Faith Estim.title: Financial Responsibility, Insurance and Good Faith Estimate Information
Financial Agreement and Good Faith Estim.summary: Payment or the applicable copay is due on the date of service. Review your plan-specific session amount and the 24-hour cancellation policy before scheduling; no undisclosed dollar amount is created by this acknowledgment.

parts.heading: Fees and payment
paragraphs: The practice reports that session charges are usually based on the reasonable-and-customary or allowed amount determined under the patient’s insurance arrangement. The actual rate and the patient’s responsibility depend on the service, payer contract, coverage, deductible, coinsurance and benefit determination. Ask the office for the specific amount applicable to the scheduled service; there is no single dollar rate supplied in this form. Self-pay or noncovered service rates must be disclosed separately before service.

Full payment, or the applicable copay when insurance is used, is due on the date of the session. Deductible, coinsurance or other lawful balances that are not known until the plan processes a claim will be explained in an itemized statement. You may ask about a bill or request correction of an error. This form does not authorize an undisclosed charge, automatic card debit, waiver of coverage rights or payment that a payer contract or law prohibits.

Cancellation at least 24 hours before the scheduled appointment start carries no cancellation charge. With less than 24 hours’ notice, the full previously disclosed session fee is due to the extent allowed by applicable law and the patient’s payer contract. A missed appointment without the required notice is subject to that policy. The practice must tell you the applicable amount and confirm that such a charge is permitted; this is not assumed to be only the copay. Missed-appointment charges are not billed as a completed clinical service, and insurance payment is not assumed. Contact the office promptly about cancellations or questions.

The practice will apply any legally required or payer-required exception and will explain charges for records, reports, testing, court-related work or other nonstandard services in advance when applicable. The form does not invent a fixed evaluation rate or require payment of an undisclosed cancellation penalty. Any payer rule that prohibits a member charge or requires uniform missed-appointment charges overrides inconsistent full-fee wording.

parts.heading: Health insurance and third-party payment
paragraphs: Insurance benefits, network status, copays, coinsurance, deductibles, referrals, prior authorizations and covered visit limits vary. Information entered in intake is patient-reported and is not a guarantee of payment. Contact your health plan and the practice to verify the relevant benefit and any prior-authorization requirements.

Claims submitted to an insurer may contain diagnoses, service dates and other information needed for payment; associated disclosures follow law and the privacy notice. Benefits may be denied or adjusted by the plan. Your actual obligation will be assessed under the plan and disclosed practice policies, not an assumed amount in this packet.

parts.heading: Self-pay rights and Good Faith Estimates
paragraphs: If you are uninsured or choose not to use insurance, federal No Surprises Act rules generally provide a right to a written Good Faith Estimate of expected charges when you schedule sufficiently in advance or request one. A Good Faith Estimate is not this financial acknowledgment. The practice must deliver any legally required estimate separately with applicable itemization and timing.

If a qualifying final bill is substantially higher than the Good Faith Estimate, federal patient-provider dispute resolution rights may apply. See cms.gov/medical-bill-rights or contact the practice. You may request a Good Faith Estimate before deciding to begin care.

parts.heading: Acknowledgment and matters requiring clarification
paragraphs: By selecting that I reviewed this information and signing below, I acknowledge the payment timing and cancellation policy described here and the obligation to obtain my applicable written rate information. The office must supply and explain the actual session amount and other charge terms before they are treated as agreed. My signature is not agreement to an undisclosed dollar amount, an automatic credit-card charge, an assignment of benefits, arbitration or waiver of the right to question a bill. If I request clarification, the office will review my questions before a disputed financial term is treated as agreed.

For uninsured or self-pay care, request the written Good Faith Estimate when scheduling or before care. When the federal process applies, a bill at least $400 above the estimate from a provider may qualify for dispute review; a request generally must begin within 120 calendar days of the initial bill. This acknowledgment is neither an individualized estimate nor a guarantee of insurer payment.

Telehealth Informed Consent.title: Optional Telehealth Informed Consent
Telehealth Informed Consent.summary: Telehealth is a choice; declining this form does not withdraw consent to available in-person counseling.

parts.heading: Nature, advantages and limits of remote care
paragraphs: Telehealth may use secure interactive video or another clinically appropriate remote modality to deliver counseling while you and the clinician are at different locations. Benefits may include convenience and access; limitations may include lost nonverbal cues, technical interruption, reduced privacy or clinical situations that call for in-person or emergency care.

At each telehealth visit, you may be asked to confirm your identity, current physical location, callback number and an emergency contact or local emergency option. Treatment across state lines is subject to clinician authorization and the law where you are physically located. The clinician may recommend in-person treatment or stop a remote visit if safe or clinically appropriate care cannot be provided.

parts.heading: Privacy, technology and emergencies
paragraphs: Use a private location, a device you control, a reliable connection and headphones if helpful. Inform the clinician if anyone else is present. Remote communications carry residual privacy and technology risks despite safeguards; notify the practice promptly of connection or privacy concerns.

If a connection fails, attempt to reconnect using the agreed visit method; call the practice at 913-353-6116 for nonemergency follow-up. For immediate danger, call 911 or local emergency services where you are. Neither participant may record a session unless the practice has separately obtained appropriate permission and applicable law permits it.

parts.heading: Voluntary authorization
paragraphs: Telehealth consent may be refused or withdrawn and does not require consent to audio/video recording, marketing, AI processing beyond disclosed treatment systems, or the release of psychotherapy notes. Ask the office about available in-person alternatives. Kansas law applies the same confidentiality and professional standards to telemedicine as to comparable in-person services.

parts.heading: Decision and withdrawal
paragraphs: A Yes decision and dated signature authorize clinically appropriate telehealth only. A No decision or request for discussion is recorded without creating telehealth consent. Discuss acceptable technology, identity and location checks, emergency procedures, accessibility needs and available alternatives with the clinician before the first remote visit. Withdrawing telehealth consent does not itself withdraw consent to a separately agreed in-person service.

Electronic Communications and Patient Po.title: Electronic Communications, Portal and E-Signature Terms
Electronic Communications and Patient Po.summary: Your separate communication preferences in this intake control whether calls, voicemail, text and ordinary email are permitted.

parts.heading: Use of electronic systems
paragraphs: The patient portal is intended for registration, appointments, intake, permitted record exchange and routine administrative communications. You must protect your password and second factor and avoid shared devices when entering private health information. Notify the practice if you suspect unauthorized account use.

Email, text messages and voicemail may be read by people who have access to the destination account or device. You may opt out of those channels, designate a confidential alternative, or restrict what may be included. Ordinary email and SMS are not assumed to be safe for sensitive clinical details. Contact preferences are recorded separately rather than presumed from this agreement.

parts.heading: Electronic documents and signatures
paragraphs: You may request paper copies, ask questions, and discuss whether non-electronic alternatives are available. Typing your legal name in the designated signature box with an affirmative acknowledgment records your intent to sign the identified document; it does not waive legal rights that require separate authorization.

The practice preserves submitted answers and signature information according to applicable retention and confidentiality duties. The site is not monitored for emergencies. Routine electronic consent does not authorize recording sessions, publicity, sale of information or disclosure to a third party.

parts.heading: Access, copies and changing this choice
paragraphs: To use electronic intake, you need a device and browser capable of displaying the pages and, to keep a PDF, a way to print or save PDF files. Request an accessible format or paper alternative if needed. You may retain each completed form using its Print / Save PDF control. Keep downloaded records in a private location.

Choosing electronic intake does not authorize every communication channel. The separate contact-preference answers govern routine email, text, voicemail and other channels. You may ask the office to change future delivery preferences, update contact details, withdraw agreement to future electronic delivery or obtain a paper copy without revoking an earlier completed authorization merely because its copy was electronic. A final electronic submission signature concerns this intake; paper preference for future documents is a separate choice.

Authorization to share health informatio.title: Optional Authorization to Use or Disclose Health Information
Authorization to share health informatio.summary: This is separate from the privacy-notice acknowledgment and informed consent. Choose No to decline without losing access to treatment.

parts.heading: Scope and specificity
paragraphs: If you select Yes, identify the person or organization authorized to disclose the information, the recipient, the specific record categories, any exclusions, purpose, direction of exchange and an expiration date or event. The practice will not treat a blank scope as a valid blanket authorization. This authorization does not include separately maintained psychotherapy notes.

Authorization is voluntary. Treatment and payment ordinarily may not be conditioned on signing it, subject to narrow exceptions in the law. You may revoke it in writing by contacting Indian Creek Psychological Services, Inc., 15022 W. 128th St., Olathe, KS 66062, except for disclosures already made in reasonable reliance on it or other applicable exceptions. Once received by certain recipients, records may be redisclosed and no longer protected by HIPAA; stricter laws may still apply.

Certain substance-use disorder records governed by 42 CFR Part 2 require a specialized compliant consent and cannot be assumed covered by an ordinary release. Ask the practice to review those requirements before such records are shared.

parts.heading: Signature, copy and effect
paragraphs: A Yes selection is effective as a recorded authorization only with completed disclosure details, a dated signature by the patient or authorized representative, and any required description of representative authority. You may receive a copy. The practice must review the scope, current validity, revocation, applicable law and destination before any disclosure. A No selection records a declined optional authorization and requires no authorization signature.

This general form excludes separately maintained psychotherapy notes and separately protected SUD counseling notes. It does not supply consent for a legal proceeding against a patient or eliminate any separate Part 2 requirement. An incoming provider’s acceptance of a two-way request is not guaranteed; that provider may require its own lawful process.

Optional consent for Part 2 substance-us.title: Separate Consent for 42 CFR Part 2 Substance-Use Disorder Records
Optional consent for Part 2 substance-us.summary: Indian Creek reports that it is not a Part 2 program. This form is not required for routine practice intake. Use only after office review confirms that identified outside records or a specific disclosure are subject to Part 2.

parts.heading: When this form is relevant to this practice
paragraphs: Indian Creek has reported that it does not operate a program subject to 42 CFR Part 2. Merely reporting alcohol or drug use does not make this form required. You may leave it unanswered or choose No for routine intake.

Records received from an outside Part 2 program can retain special protections even when the receiving practice is not itself a Part 2 program. The office must determine whether the identified records and proposed use or disclosure are covered before requesting or relying on this separate consent. No disclosure is authorized by a blank form.

parts.heading: Your separate choice and protected information
paragraphs: Certain records identifying a person as receiving substance-use disorder services from a federally assisted Part 2 program are protected by 42 CFR Part 2. If this rule applies, the practice or other holder generally needs a compliant written consent or a recognized exception before sharing such information.

If you choose Yes, identify the specific program or holder that may disclose, the specific recipient or qualifying class of recipients, what records may be shared, the purpose, and an expiration date or event. You may choose a treatment/payment/health-care-operations consent where the rule permits it, or a different specific purpose. Do not sign a form with incomplete disclosure details.

A lawful Part 2 consent does not automatically authorize using your records in civil, criminal, administrative or legislative proceedings against you. An appropriate separate consent or qualifying court order and legal process are required. If a HIPAA-regulated recipient receives Part 2 records under an authorized treatment/payment/operations consent, subsequent disclosures may be governed by HIPAA while special legal-proceedings restrictions continue.

parts.heading: Voluntary authorization, revocation and other protected notes
paragraphs: You may decline this authorization. You may revoke a valid consent in writing through the identified disclosing program or the practice, subject to lawful reliance and exceptions. Certain downstream redisclosures may occur under the governing regulations; discuss those implications before signing.

This consent does not authorize disclosure of separately maintained Part 2 SUD counseling notes. Such notes, if applicable, require their own separate authorization under the specific rules. The office must review every completed Part 2 request for scope and applicability before releasing information.

parts.heading: Applicability and separate legal-proceeding requests
paragraphs: The office must first determine whether the identified program or records are subject to Part 2; a report of alcohol or drug use on an intake does not itself answer that question. This general Part 2 form is not combined with a consent for civil, criminal, administrative or legislative investigation or proceedings against the patient. Such a request requires its own legally sufficient process.

A No decision requires no authorization signature. A Yes decision requires the complete scope, purpose, recipient, expiration and dated signature and remains subject to office review before use. The signature is not permission to disclose separately maintained SUD counseling notes or psychotherapy notes under a broad routine-care consent.

Separate consent for SUD counseling note.title: Independent Authorization for Substance-Use Disorder Counseling Notes
Separate consent for SUD counseling note.summary: Indian Creek reports that it is not a Part 2 program. This form is not required for routine practice intake. Use only after office review confirms that identified outside records or a specific disclosure are subject to Part 2.

parts.heading: When this form is relevant to this practice
paragraphs: Indian Creek has reported that it does not operate a program subject to 42 CFR Part 2. Merely reporting alcohol or drug use does not make this form required. You may leave it unanswered or choose No for routine intake.

Records received from an outside Part 2 program can retain special protections even when the receiving practice is not itself a Part 2 program. The office must determine whether the identified records and proposed use or disclosure are covered before requesting or relying on this separate consent. No disclosure is authorized by a blank form.

parts.heading: What this form covers
paragraphs: Part 2 protects separately maintained SUD counseling notes that document or analyze the contents of a conversation during a private or group SUD counseling session, as defined by the regulation. This category is distinct from ordinary SUD treatment records and also may differ from psychotherapy notes under HIPAA.

If you elect Yes, identify the holder authorized to disclose, the intended recipient, the precise notes, the purpose, expiration date or event, and provide a separately dated signature. This optional consent does not authorize disclosure of unrelated treatment information or other categories of notes.

parts.heading: Your control
paragraphs: You may choose No. A refusal is not a refusal of all substance-use treatment. You may revoke permission in writing, subject to permitted prior reliance and legal exceptions. Staff will verify record classification, legal authority and the completed authorization before making a disclosure.

parts.heading: Independent choice and dated signature
paragraphs: This consent may be combined only with another consent for SUD counseling notes where law permits; it is not bundled with ordinary treatment-record consent. Treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits may not be conditioned on signing this optional notes consent. Choose No if you do not authorize the described disclosure.

If you choose Yes, the completed scope, recipient, purpose, expiration, signature, signature date and any representative authority must be recorded. Ask for a copy. Revocation is prospective subject to lawful reliance and exceptions. Office review of applicability and the current authorization is required before any use or disclosure.

Separate authorization for psychotherapy.title: Separate, Optional Psychotherapy-Notes Authorization
Separate authorization for psychotherapy.summary: This permission is not combined with the general release, and declining it does not prevent ordinary treatment.

parts.heading: Specially protected notes and choice
paragraphs: This form concerns only psychotherapy notes as defined by HIPAA: notes kept separately from the medical record that document or analyze session conversations. They are not the routine progress notes, diagnosis, dates, treatment plans or billing records that may be kept in the designated record set.

Select Yes only after identifying the party authorized to disclose the notes, the receiving party, precise purpose, expiration date or event, and the individual or authorized representative signing. Authorization is voluntary; most uses and disclosures of psychotherapy notes require this separate form, apart from limited legal exceptions.

You can revoke authorization in writing through the practice, except to the extent already relied upon or as otherwise provided by law. Disclosure may lead to redisclosure outside HIPAA protection, subject to other applicable law.

parts.heading: Scope, separate signature and no condition of treatment
paragraphs: Describe the particular separately maintained psychotherapy notes to be disclosed, the discloser, recipient, purpose and expiration, and sign and date this form separately if you choose Yes. If you choose No, no authorization signature is required. This optional notes authorization is not a condition of routine treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits except where a specific lawful exception applies.

Ask for a copy and contact the practice to revoke prospectively in writing, subject to prior lawful reliance and exceptions. An uploaded or printed copy does not itself verify authority, authenticity, current validity, or permission for a disclosure; staff must review those matters before use.

Patient attestation and consent to submi.title: Final Patient Declaration and Electronic Signature
Patient attestation and consent to submi.summary: Each optional authorization remains independent. This final signature confirms information accuracy and the intended electronic submission.

parts.heading: What your signature means
paragraphs: I have had an opportunity to read the documents in this packet, request a paper copy, identify unanswered questions and make separate choices about treatment, payment information, telehealth and optional releases. No single final signature substitutes for a missing authorization required under federal or Kansas law.

I understand that knowingly false information can affect assessment, insurance or treatment planning. Information I provide is true and complete to the best of my knowledge; I may notify the practice about needed corrections. I understand the practice may need to resolve requests for discussion or unsigned consent forms before the relevant service is provided.

I understand that choosing not to authorize a separate release of records or psychotherapy notes does not by itself bar care. The electronic signature below records intent to submit this intake and the selected acknowledgments.

parts.heading: Intent, copies and corrections
paragraphs: I intend the name I type and date on this final page to be my electronic signature for submission of the information and independent decisions recorded in this intake. I am signing as the patient or in the representative capacity I have identified. I have not signed another person’s name without lawful authority.

I may keep a copy of each form. Before submitting I can return to any page, change a decision, correct information or ask the office for assistance. After submission the original record is retained; later corrections or revocations are documented separately and do not erase what was originally recorded.

This final attestation does not transform a declined release into an authorization, a paper-delivery preference into consent to unrestricted electronic contact, an unverified representative into a guardian, or an unsigned conditional form into an effective consent. Choosing not to sign an optional disclosure does not by itself refuse care.

Legal Representative and Minor Consent.title: Legal Representative, Minor Consent and Authority to Act
Legal Representative and Minor Consent.summary: Complete and sign the representative portion only when acting for the patient. Authority must be reviewed by the practice; family relationship or a document upload alone does not establish it.

parts.heading: Identify the patient, signer and authority
paragraphs: When a person signs for a patient, identify that person by full legal name, relationship, contact information and the specific legal authority relied upon, such as a court appointment, applicable parental authority or a health-care decision-making instrument. Describe relevant limits, expiration, shared-decision requirements or restrictions. Supply applicable custody, guardianship or foster-placement papers through the assignment-upload section on page 2 or directly to the office.

The practice must assess the authority and scope before relying on the signature. Foster placement, emergency-contact status, being a spouse or relative, paying for treatment, or possessing a patient portal login does not by itself confer unrestricted authority to consent to care or receive records. This form does not create guardianship or change an existing court order.

parts.heading: Minors and limits on representative access
paragraphs: Consent and record-access rights depend on the patient’s circumstances and applicable law. Some services or information may be controlled by a minor or another legally authorized decision-maker. Do not assume a parent or guardian can sign every release or access every confidential detail. The clinician and office must review court orders, relevant consent rules, the patient’s capacity and any applicable protections before services or disclosures.

Where participation by a minor is appropriate, the clinician will explain treatment and confidentiality in an understandable way and seek the minor’s participation or assent as appropriate. Assent does not replace any legally required consent, and a representative’s signature does not waive rights the representative lacks authority to waive.

parts.heading: Representative declaration
paragraphs: If I sign as representative, I state that the authority I describe is accurate to the best of my knowledge, I will provide supporting information requested by the practice, and I will promptly report relevant changes or restrictions. I understand my signature is accepted as a recorded assertion of authority pending office review, not independent legal verification.

If the patient signs for themself and no representative is needed, the representative signature and date may remain blank. This page records no additional authorization to disclose records: optional releases on later pages must still be separately completed by the person legally entitled to authorize them.

Obtain agreement for electronic workflow; keep individual contact-channel choices separate and offer a paper alternative.

Provide the notice and make a good-faith acknowledgment effort. A patient may decline acknowledgment without being denied care for that reason.

forms.when: Indian Creek reports it is not a Part 2 program. Not required for routine intake; use only after office review of applicable outside protected records. A blank or No choice gives no authorization.
